result.note: Tests the May 2026 customs duty hike on gold and silver, its forex rationale, and India's position as a gold consumer. The record discount, a market move, is skipped.

questions.prompt: In May 2026, India raised the import duty on gold and silver from 6% to what rate?
questions.explain: On 13 May 2026, India raised import duties on gold and silver from 6% to 15%. The hike came days after PM Modi urged citizens to pause gold purchases for a year to conserve foreign exchange.
questions.source: On Wednesday, India hiked import duties on gold and silver from 6% to 15%, a drastic move to shore up foreign exchange reserves as geopolitical instability rattles the rupee.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India and gold, in the context of the import duty hike of May 2026:
items: The duty hike was intended to shore up India's foreign exchange reserves.
India is the world's largest consumer of gold.
Indian gold demand is driven largely by investments and jewellery.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: India is the world's second-largest gold consumer, not the largest, so statement 2 is wrong. The hike aimed to protect foreign exchange reserves as geopolitical instability weighed on the rupee.
questions.source: India is the world’s second-largest gold consumer, with demand largely driven by investments and jewellery.
